text:
Sanjay Patel: Heads up — started getting alerts that a handful of users can't finish SSO login this morning. Looks correlated with yesterday's RBAC change that made `department` required for JIT provisioning.
Emily Chen: seeing same. Affected users show 'Missing required attribute: department' in the IdP SAML response logs.
Sanjay Patel: Ugh. Did we land that change in the org role policy yesterday? I thought it was behind a feature flag.
Michael V: I rolled the policy to require department for new hires only, but apparently the rollout rule was mis-tagged and applied org-wide. My bad. :grimacing:
Emily Chen: can we hotfix to accept empty department for existing accounts? We need logins restored fast.
Ara K: FYI Okta Bot shows provisioning failures for ~42 users between 04:12 and 04:47 UTC. Also noticed our audit pipeline didn't ingest the Okta provisioning webhook for some of them — gap in audit logs.
Security Oncall: @Emily Chen @Michael V please provide the exact error message and a sample SAML assertion for an affected user (sanitized). We need to confirm whether it's attribute absence vs empty string.
Okta Bot: automated note: webhook delivery attempt 3 failed to audit-service (504 gateway). Payloads queued for retry.
Emily Chen: sample error: "JIT_PROVISION_FAILED: missing attribute 'department'". Sample SAML snippet (sanitized): ```<Attribute Name="department"></Attribute>``` — present but empty.
Sanjay Patel: so Okta is sending the attribute but blank, our provisioning rejects blank as missing. Proposed emergency plan: 1) revert policy change that enforces non-empty department for existing users, 2) patch provisioning code to treat empty string as null for now, 3) replay webhook audit events once audit-service is back.
Michael V: I can rollback the policy in 2 mins. Also will add a canary check to ensure only the targeted group gets the enforcement.
Security Oncall: rollback approved. Emily, once rollback is done, can you confirm login success for 10 affected users? Also open an incident ticket for the audit gap and tag SRE.
Emily Chen: rollback complete. Confirmed logins succeed for 9/10 in my sample set, one still failing (edge case). Captured SAML for that one — department attribute missing entirely.
Ara K: saved failing user ID and SAML to secure incident doc. Also the audit-service 504 was due to the newer KMS client we deployed last week failing on key rotation call — caused webhook ingestion delays and retries overflow.
Sanjay Patel: KMS rotation? Which key? That's cosmetic or could block replay of audit events.
Ara K: rotation for audit-service envelope key (kms-audit-prod). Rotation started automatic window at 04:05 UTC, client attempted a rewrap and saw IAM permissions mismatch for the new key alias.
Michael V: that's a config issue on the audit-service role; I pushed a fix to grant decrypt/wrap with the new alias. Requesting a manual replay of queued webhook payloads after confirm.
Security Oncall: action items: - Michael: verify IAM and KMS alias permissions and confirm rotation succeeded (ETA 15m) - Emily: validate full list of affected users and confirm logins after rollback (ETA 10m) - Ara: preserve original webhook payloads in incident bucket and do not purge - Sanjay: add a short retrospective note on rollout flagging and add a preflight test for attribute enforcement.
Emily Chen: quick note — we should also add a defensive fallback in provisioning: if department empty or missing, map to 'unknown-dept' and create minimal role mapping to avoid privilege escalation.
Sanjay Patel: agree. After rollbacks/repairs, let's ship the fallback + unit tests behind a flag, then re-run rollout targeting new-hire group only.
Okta Bot: audit-service webhook queue drained after KMS fix and manual replay initiated.
Security Oncall: Incident created: INC-2026-0421. I'll follow up with postmortem template. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
